templateSummaries.Front Desk Nursery: Task-first. Key facts (ages, hours, funded hours, places, grades) and answers up front. Needs no photos of people.
templateSummaries.Key Worker: People-led. The team and key workers are the brand. Needs consented staff portraits.
templateSummaries.Garden Gate: Place-led. Walk from the gate to the garden, room by room. Needs 10 or more good premises photos.
templateSummaries.Cut and Stick: Playful cut paper, Scottish wildlife stickers and a noticeboard of proof. Playgroups and nature-loving nurseries.
templateSummaries.Full Stop: Bold colour blocks and big type for working parents: "your week, sorted". Large, long-hours nurseries.
templateSummaries.Chapter One: Settling in told as a storybook, with drawn scenes. Home-from-home nurseries with baby rooms; works with no photos.
templateSummaries.Weatherproof: A strong outdoors brand: outside every day, whatever the weather. Forest and outdoor nurseries.
templateSummaries.Big Table: Food and family: this week's lunches on a recipe card, the cook by name. Nurseries that cook on site.
templateSummaries.Sidekick: Mascot-led and very colourful: a drawn animal guide in every section, highlighted words, clock-box hours. Few photos needed.
templateSummaries.Make Waves: Bright colour bands with wave seams and a drawn local theme (sea, river, hills or city). Big-number facts, ringed photos.
templateSummaries.Meadow: Light and painterly: a watercolour scene, blob photo collage with a living photo, one-word tiles. Farm, rural and small nurseries.

stages.name: Targets
stages.description: Websites found by the discovery task, waiting to be analysed.
stages.instructions: Discovery: find websites of independent (private or voluntary) nurseries in Scotland and add them with `node pipeline/cli.mjs add <url> --name "<nursery>"` (or `import <file>` for a list). Council nurseries and chains with their own web teams aren't targets. Duplicates are skipped automatically. You don't claim cards here; Analysis pulls from this bucket.

stages.name: Analysis
stages.description: Study each site and score it 1–10.
stages.instructions: Open the site and judge it as a potential redesign client, from a parent's point of view on a phone. Score it 1–10 on design, mobile layout, speed, how quickly a parent finds the answers they need (ages, hours, funded hours, fees, places, inspection grades, how to visit or join), calls to action, trust signals (real staff, real rooms and garden, the inspection report) and how dated it looks (1 = very poor, 10 = excellent). Set `score` and write `analysis` (3–6 short bullet points backing the score). Rating follows the score (1–4 bad, 5–7 average, 8–10 good) unless you set `rating` yourself. Then complete the card; it moves to the matching bucket.

stages.name: Bad sites
stages.description: Highest-priority sales targets. Redesign study pulls from here first.

stages.name: Average sites
stages.description: Second-priority targets. Pulled once Bad sites is empty.

stages.name: Good sites
stages.description: Not targeted. Parked here for reference.

stages.name: Needs attention
stages.description: Cards an AI worker couldn't finish. Read why on the card, sort it out, then drag it to the right bucket.

stages.name: Redesign study
stages.description: Work out what needs to change and which template to use.
stages.instructions:
Read the nursery research brief first (you're given the path). Its rules on facts, photos of children and structure apply to every nursery site.

Before you start, the nursery's current website has been crawled for you (every page, its navigation, photos and documents; see the source-site overview and files). Read every page with real content, look at the photos, and open any leaflets, menus and handbooks. The homepage alone misses most of what the nursery publishes. The card's notes hold its Care Inspectorate record: places, whether it takes under 3s, the manager and its latest grades.

Write `findings`: (1) the concrete problems with the current site (layout, mobile, speed, out-of-date notices, pop-ups, carousels, PDF-only menus or forms, Facebook-only updates, broken or missing pages, weak calls to action); (2) a content inventory: what each existing page says that a parent needs (ages and rooms, hours and closures, funded hours and partner-provider status, fees, places and the waiting list, how to visit, settling in, a day at nursery, outdoor play, food and allergies, the team and qualifications, the inspection report, policies, parents' information, jobs), noting anything out of date or contradicting the Scottish rules in the research brief (for example the old 2022 quality framework headings, or grades that don't match the notes); (3) which real photos exist and what they show (staff, rooms, garden, building, children's work, food), with their file names in source/img. List separately every photo that shows an identifiable child: those are excluded from the new site.

Choose a `template` by what the nursery is and what it has. Go by its real character on its current site, not its name: a nursery whose name or logo is an animal or creature (bee, owl, bear, ladybird...) and that wants a bright, playful look gets "Sidekick"; one in a place with a strong local identity (coast, river, hills, city) that wants a big, bright brand gets "Make Waves"; a small farm, rural or owner-run nursery with good photos of its animals, garden or outdoors gets "Meadow"; a fully outdoor or forest nursery gets "Weatherproof"; one that cooks on site and publishes a menu or names its cook gets "Big Table"; a large nursery with long hours that sells to working parents gets "Full Stop"; a playgroup or nature-loving nursery with a playful voice (or creature-named rooms) gets "Cut and Stick"; a small home-from-home nursery with a baby room, especially one with few usable photos, gets "Chapter One"; a nursery whose current site has good, consistent photos of its own staff (with names and roles) gets "Key Worker"; one whose best photos show its building, rooms and garden (10 or more usable ones without identifiable children) gets "Garden Gate"; any other nursery gets "Front Desk Nursery". Say in `findings` which photos exist and why you chose the template. Read the template's BRIEF.md (you're given the path).

Write `pages`: the site map of the new site, using the research brief's 6-item menu (Home, Visit and join, Fees and funding, Our nursery, Our team, Parents) and dropping pages the nursery has no content for. For each page give: its title, a short URL like `fees-and-funding.html`, its purpose, the sections it contains, which source pages (pages/NN-slug.md) its content comes from, and which photos (source/img files) it uses. Keep the main menu to 7 items or fewer. End with a short list of existing content you're deliberately leaving out and why (for example stale COVID notices, old fees with no date, photos of identifiable children). Nothing a parent needs may be lost.

Write `plan`: the homepage section by section, and how the template is themed for this nursery (logo, colours from the logo, which photos go where), what to keep and what to add. Mark every fact that must be confirmed with the nursery (funded status, fees, places, hours) as "phone to check" unless the current site states it.

Then complete with outcome `done`.

If the nursery has no working website (the site is down, doesn't load, is only a Facebook page, or the card links to its Care Inspectorate record), don't give up: this is a prospect for a brand-new site. Gather what you can from the crawl, the Care Inspectorate details in the notes and a web search: name, address, phone, ages, hours, funded status, team and photos. In `findings`, say there's no working website and list what you found. Choose a `template` (usually Front Desk Nursery), write a `pages` site map (usually a smaller one) and a `plan` for a new site built from those details. Then complete with outcome `new_site`.

stages.name: Ready to build
stages.description: Site, findings and redesign plan, waiting for a builder.

stages.name: Build
stages.description: Design the new site on the chosen template.
stages.instructions:
Build the redesign on the chosen `template`, following `findings`, `plan` and the nursery research brief. Read the template's BRIEF.md and its worked example first (you're given the paths), copy its styles.css into the site unchanged except for the custom properties at the top, and follow the example's homepage structure and quality bar. Reuse the nursery's real content, logo and brand colours. If the card was planned as a new site (there's no working website), build it from the details gathered in `findings`, `plan` and the notes. Never invent fees, places, funded status, grades, ratios, staff, qualifications, menus, hours, reviews or policies: write "phone to check" instead, as the research brief's table says. Show every Care Inspectorate grade from the card's notes, with the date and a link to the report, never only the best one. The grade names in the notes come from the Care Inspectorate datastore; reports published since 22 September 2025 use the shared inspection framework's headings (see the research brief), so use the report's exact headings when the nursery's site or report states them, and otherwise say in your note that the headings need checking. Deploy a preview and set `previewUrl`. If the card came back from review, address everything in `review` first. Then complete the card.

Build every page listed in `pages`, not just the homepage. Every page uses the same header, footer, navigation, tokens and components as the template's example, with one h1, a short intro and clear sections; mark the current page in the menu. Take each page's content from the source pages named in `pages` (source/pages/NN-slug.md): rewrite it in plain English at a reading age of 9 to 11, but keep every fact, and never add facts that aren't there. Put menus, forms and policies in HTML, not only as PDFs. Copy the photos named in `pages` and `plan` from source/img into site/img, resize them sensibly, strip their metadata, and write real alt text. Never use a photo that shows an identifiable child, and never use stock or AI-generated people. No pop-ups, carousels, social feeds, map embeds or trackers. The waiting list is "phone or email us" unless the nursery already has a form service. Link pages with relative links (`fees-and-funding.html`). Run the audit on the finished site: it crawls every page. Previews are sandboxed, so never reference SVG drawings in another file with `<use href="file.svg#id">` (it draws nothing): put the SVG sprite inline in each page and use `<use href="#id">`.

stages.name: AI review
stages.description: An agent checks the build against the plan and template.
stages.instructions:
A browser audit of the preview runs just before you start (every link clicked, axe accessibility to WCAG 2.1 AA, phone layout and tap targets, menu, forms, keyboard), and you get its report and screenshots. Treat its measurements as facts. Then judge what it can't: compare `previewUrl` with the original `url`, the `findings`, the `plan`, the chosen `template`'s BRIEF.md rules (you're given the path) and the nursery research brief. Check every planned section exists, the nursery's real content (name, phone, address, hours, ages, fees, funded status, team) was carried over correctly, the Care Inspectorate grades match the card's notes exactly (every grade, the date and a report link), and nothing is invented or placeholder. Open every image in site/img: any identifiable child, or any stock or AI-generated person, is a failure. Write `review`: one line on what you checked, then a numbered list of everything to fix, most important first, each specific enough for the builder (which page and element, and what to change). Complete with outcome `changes` if there is any audit blocker or major issue, a missing planned section, invented or placeholder content, wrong grades, or a photo of an identifiable child; otherwise `pass`, listing any minor issues in the review. External links the audit couldn't verify aren't failures.

Also check the whole site against `pages` and the source-site inventory: every planned page exists and is linked, each one carries the facts from its source pages (spot-check fees, hours, names, qualifications and phone numbers against source/pages), and nothing a parent needs from the old site was lost. A missing planned page or lost parent information means outcome `changes`.

stages.name: Human review
stages.description: Final sign-off before the site goes to sales.

stages.name: Ready to pitch
stages.description: Approved redesigns. Pitch with the before and after.
stages.instructions: Contact the nursery (usually the manager or owner) and show the original site (`url`) next to the redesign (`previewUrl`). Before you pitch, confirm the facts marked "phone to check". Record who you spoke to in `contact` and what you said in `pitchNotes`.

stages.name: Interested
stages.description: Wants to go ahead. Hand over to closing.
